newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-CHRISTIE REPLACED BY WILLIAMS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-CHRISTIE REPLACED BY WILLIAMS.

text.p: John Williams was on Saturday reinstated as Northern Transvaal coach, replacing former World Cup team chief Kitch Christie -- the man who took his job at the beginning of the season.
It was announced at Ellis Park that Christie has resigned due to ill health.
The move comes after a string of poor results in the Super 12 tournament.
Northerns lost all four of their matches in New Zealand and Australia before snatching a 16-16 draw against Gauteng Lions on Saturday.
Christie's assistant coach Uli Schmidt told a news conference: "The guys went out there to play their hearts out for Kitch."
The replacement of the man who coached South Africa to their 1995 World Cup triumph may plunge the Northerns camp into crisis again.
Before the Super 12 season began, Williams was replaced by Christie after three years in charge following a players' revolt.
Senior players accused Williams of being out of touch with the modern game and the arrival of Christie was a direct result of the players' request for a more enlightened coach.
But Christie, who has long suffered from cancer, was unable to travel with the team abroad due to ill health. He is currently in hospital in Pretoria suffering from pneumonia.
